title: Delhi ward and district profiles: export bundle

geographies.caveat: Legacy ward geography (DataMeet, CC-BY-SA 2.5 India), before the 2022 delimitation; not an official or current boundary.
Simplified boundaries (about 165 m tolerance), not survey-grade.

nullPolicy: A blank cell means the source does not hold the figure. It is never zero. A zero is a source zero, or a count of mapped features that found none (read the uncertainty class).
cannotEstablish: Why crashes happened, or that any facility here caused or would prevent them.
Risk per person or per trip: there are no pedestrian or traffic counts, so counts are not rates of risk.
That a place without mapped infrastructure has none: OpenStreetMap coverage is uneven.
Crime by ward: crime is published only for the 15 police districts.
Anything about the current 250 MCD wards: these profiles use the legacy 290-ward geography.
A change over time for a ward or a named zone: boundaries, zone lists and mapping all change between years.
Who is responsible for a location, or what should be built there. Field verification is needed before any intervention.
licences: OpenStreetMap-derived fields: OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL 1.0 (attribution required).
Ward boundaries: DataMeet Municipal_Spatial_Data, CC-BY-SA 2.5 India (share-alike applies to the ward GeoJSON).
Official figures (NCRB, Delhi Traffic Police, Delhi Police): no open reuse licence has been verified for the source documents.

Delhi Metro gate locations: Delhi Metro Rail Corporation, via the Delhi Transport Stack (Department of Transport, GNCTD), dataset 3, version 1, last updated by the publisher 2024-12-02. Counts and distances here were derived by this project and are not the original data. Provided without warranty; neither DMRC nor the Delhi Transport Stack guarantees its accuracy. Licence: Delhi Transport Stack Licence Agreement 1.0 (derivatives allowed; the gate file itself is not redistributed here).
methodNotes: Counts are assigned to wards by point-in-polygon; footway length by segment midpoint. Points on a boundary go to the first ward that contains them.
Crash-zone fields depend on hand-placed positions with stated accuracy of 150 m to 5 km; the ward a zone falls in can be wrong.
District profiles carry the 2023 to 2024 comparability state from data/continuity.json; no change figure is calculated.
